note.question: How do key drivers of optimal designs include the assay cost function, the tester’s preference toward cost and capacity efficiency, prevalence/coinfection rates, and for the robust model, prevalence uncertainty compare?
note.overview: Infectious disease screening can be expensive and capacity constrained. The paper develops costand capacity-efficient testing designs for multidisease screening, considering (1) multiplexing (disease bundling), where one assay detects multiple diseases using the same specimen (e.g., nasal swabs, blood), and (2) pooling (specimen bundling), where one assay is used on specimens from multiple subjects bundled in a testing pool. A testing design specifies an assay portfolio (mix of single-disease/multiplex assays) and a testing method (pooling/individual testing per assay).
